blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from individual human demonstrations. We present FineDex, a framework that makes finger-level intent both expressible and executable. FineDex learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions on hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects. To bridge generation and execution, FineDex leverages generated interactions as actionable priors for an agent that discovers physically feasible contact strategies through practice in a physics-based digital twin. By adapting at test time without per-instance retraining, FineDex generalizes across fine-grained instructions and object configurations. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art HOI generation quality and fine-grained controllability, substantial improvements in dexterous manipulation success, and successful deployment on a real dexterous humanoid robot.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control: humans press with a fingertip,
hook with a specific finger, brace with the palm, and switch hands when one is busy.
Yet existing dexterous manipulation and human–object interaction (HOI)
generation methods are evaluated mainly by task completion
alone: many effectively use a five-fingered hand as a gripper for
pick-and-place [ 25 , 28 ] ,
while others copy whatever finger usage appears in a specific human
demonstration [ 7 , 24 ] . Meanwhile, human interaction data offers a scalable source of rich
finger-level behaviors. The missing link is a model that can express such intent
on demand—which hand, which finger, which contact—and a way to realize it on a physical robot.
blocks.zh:
Dexterity的核心是手指控制: 人类用指尖按住,
用特定的手指勾住,用手掌扣住,在一个人忙的时候可以换手。
然而,现有的人为操纵和人为交互作用(HOI)
主要通过任务完成来评价生成方法
单是:许多人有效地用一手五指来抓
取出位置 [25, 28],
而其他人复制任何 手指用法出现在特定的人类
[7、24]。 同时,人类互动数据提供了可扩展的丰富来源
指层行为. 缺失的链接是能够表达这种意图的模型
需要时——哪只手,哪只手指,哪只手指接触—— 以及用物理机器人实现的方法。

blocks.en:
However, existing methods fall short on both fronts. On the expression side, text-conditioned HOI generators
synthesize coordinated human–object motion [ 3 , 23 , 1 , 21 ] ,
but they respond almost only to task-level descriptions: asked to use the left hand or a
particular finger, they produce the same interaction regardless. On the realization side,
generated motions are not physically exact, and differences
in robot kinematics and contact dynamics make direct
motion replay unreliable. Existing pipelines bridge this gap by training
reference-tracking policies [ 7 , 4 ] ,
but their reliance on reference-specific training
limits scalability to diverse fine-grained instructions,
object configurations, and robot-specific constraints.
blocks.zh:
然而,现有的方法在两方面都不足。 在表达式方面,文本条件为HOI的生成器
合成经协调的人体-物体运动[3、23、1、21],
但是它们几乎只回应任务级别描述: 要求使用左手或一个
特别的手指,不管怎样,它们产生相同的相互作用。 在实现方面,
产生的运动在物理上并不精确,而且差异
在机器人动能和接触动力学中
动作重放不可靠。 现有管道通过培训来弥补这一差距
参考跟踪政策[7、4],
但他们依赖特定参考培训
将可扩展性限制在各种精细指示上,
对象配置,以及机器人特定限制.

blocks.en:
Our key insight is to decouple fine-grained intent generation
from its physical realization, treating generated HOI
as a sketch of the intended interaction. What a human would do is best captured by a generative prior
learned from fine-grained human interaction data. How the robot can do it is best discovered through
test-time practice in a physics-based digital twin.
Generation supplies the finger-level intent;
practice supplies its physical grounding.
blocks.zh:
我们的关键洞察力是 将精致的意向产生解开
从物理实现,治疗生成的HOI
作为预期互动的草图。 人类会做的最好被先天性
从精细的人类交互数据中吸取了教训. 机器人如何做到最好通过
在基于物理学的数字双胞胎中试验时间练习.
一代人提供指层意图;
实践提供了其物理地基。

blocks.en:
Building on this observation, we introduce FineDex , a framework that makes
finger-level intent both expressible and executable. As shown in Fig. 1 , FineDex learns
to generate coordinated body, hand, and object motions
conditioned on fine-grained instructions specifying hand selection,
individual finger motions, and designated contacts. For execution, FineDex treats generated interactions as
actionable priors for an agent that proposes contact programs, practices them under
randomized dynamics, and commits to the most reliable behavior, which
is then executed on the robot. Because adaptation happens through practice, the same system
generalizes to new instructions, robot-specific constraints,
and object configurations without retraining.
blocks.zh:
基于这个观察,我们引入了 FineDex, 这个框架使得
指级意图,既可以表示,也可以执行. 如图1所示,FineDex学习
产生协调体、手和物体动议
以精细指示为条件,具体说明手的选择,
指动和指定联系人 对于执行, FineDex 将生成的相互作用视为
提出联系程序的代理人的可诉前科,按下列规定进行:
随机动态,并致力于最可靠的行为,
然后在机器人上执行。 因为适应是通过实践实现的 同一个系统
概括到新的指令,机器人特有的限制,
和不进行再培训的对象配置。

blocks.en:
To measure what task success alone cannot, we introduce FingerBench, which evaluates
whether generated motions follow hand- and finger-level instructions and whether robots
realize them in physics-based execution. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art HOI generation quality
and finger-level controllability. In physics-based execution, practice turns generated priors into reliable
contact behaviors where direct replay rarely succeeds while preserving designated finger contacts. On a real Unitree G1 humanoid, FineDex completes
articulated-object tasks under constraints it was never trained for, such as operating
with the left hand only or with a single designated finger.
blocks.zh:
为了衡量什么任务不能成功,我们引入了Finger Bench,它评价
运动是否遵循手和指级指令,以及机器人是否
在基于物理的处决中意识到它们. 实验展示了最先进的HOI生成质量
和手指水平的可控性。 在以物理为基础的执行中,实践将生成的前缀变为可靠的
联系行为,直接重放很少成功,同时保留指定的指触. 在真正的Unitree G1人相上,FineDex完成
限制下明确的目标任务,如操作
仅用左手或单指指定。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Human–Object Interaction Generation
blocks.zh: 2.1 人类-目标互动生成

blocks.en:
Text-conditioned HOI generation synthesizes coordinated hand, body, and object motion. Hand-centric methods generate contact-aware interactions through
diffusion [ 3 , 5 ] or masked autoregressive
diffusion [ 1 ] , while whole-body methods generate human–object
motion [ 14 , 13 , 21 ] . HOIDiNi [ 23 ] improves contact realism through
diffusion noise optimization, F-HOI [ 29 ] aligns fine-grained interaction states
with language, and physics-based approaches synthesize dexterous grasping and articulated
interactions [ 33 , 32 , 27 ] . Despite improved semantic and contact fidelity,
instruction-level control over hand selection and
individual finger contacts remains underexplored.
Our work addresses this gap, evaluated through FingerBench.
blocks.zh:
有文字条件 HOI一代合成了协调手,身体,和物体运动. 以手为中心的方法产生接触-意识相互作用
扩散[3, 5]或被遮住的自递性
扩散[1],而全身方法产生人-对象
[14、13、21]。 HOIDINI [23] 改善接触现实主义
扩散噪声优化 F-HOI [29] 坐标为细纹相互作用状态
和基于物理的方法 综合了非曲直的把握和表达
互动[33、32、27]。 尽管语义和接触忠贞有所改进,
指令级别对手选择的控制
个人的手指接触仍然没有得到充分利用。
我们的工作通过Finger Bench评估了这一差距。

blocks.en: 2.2 Learning Dexterity from Human Data
blocks.zh: 2.2 从人类数据中学习数据

blocks.en:
Human demonstrations provide a rich source of dexterous behavior. Retargeting methods
transfer captured or video-derived hand motion to robot
hands [ 22 , 24 , 15 , 19 , 20 ] , often refined by residual
reinforcement learning [ 7 , 15 ] , and DexMimicGen [ 12 ] scales demonstrations through trajectory generation. At the humanoid level, motion
trackers reproduce large libraries of reference behaviors [ 17 ] , and
RoboSTAR [ 31 ] transfers generated sign-language motion, including fine finger
articulation, to humanoid hands without object contact. EmbodyHOI [ 4 ] adds embodiment-aware kinematic guidance during HOI generation, while
FlowHOI [ 30 ] executes contact-aware generated HOI trajectories on robot arms.
These methods primarily inherit finger usage from reference
demonstrations, with physical execution often relying on
imitation or reference-tracking policies.
FineDex instead enables instruction-specified finger control,
grounded through test-time practice without per-reference training.
blocks.zh:
人类的示威活动为狡猾的行为提供了丰富的来源. 重新确定目标的方法
将捕获的或视频产生的手动转移给机器人
手 [22、24、15、19、20],往往由剩余
增强学习 [7, 15], 和 DexmicGen [12] 通过轨迹生成的平面演示. 在人性层面,运动
追踪器复制大型参考行为库[17],以及
RoboSTAR [31] 转会产生手语动作,包括精细的手指
发音,指无物体接触的人体手。 EmbodyHOI [4] 在HOI世代中增加了能感知到动能的指导,同时
FlowHOI [30] 在机器人手臂上执行接触意识生成的HOI轨迹.
这些方法主要继承参考文献中的指法
示威游行,往往依靠实际处决
模仿或参考跟踪政策。
FineDex可以控制指向
在不经过每一次参考培训的情况下,通过测试时间做法进行。

blocks.en: 2.3 Language-Guided Agentic Manipulation
blocks.zh: 2.3 语言指导剂操纵

blocks.en:
Language-model agents plan robot behavior through affordance-grounded skill
selection [ 11 ] , code generation [ 16 ] , and spatial or keypoint
constraints [ 10 , 9 ] . Simulation-driven approaches synthesize rewards and
tasks for policy learning [ 18 , 26 ] , and RAX [ 8 ] acquires
manipulation skills through online exploration with executable robot programs.
FineDex connects agentic planning with generative HOI priors.
blocks.zh:
语言模范特工通过付费技能规划机器人行为
选择 [11],代码生成 [16],以及空间或关键点
[10,9]. 模拟驱动的方法综合了奖励和
政策学习任务[18、26]和RAX[8]
操作技能 通过在线探索 与可执行的机器人程序。
FineDex将代理规划与基因HOI前传连接.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
As shown in Fig. 2 , FineDex decomposes finger-level manipulation into two stages. Given an articulated object 𝒪 \mathcal{O} and an
instruction ℓ \ell that may specify the acting hand, finger motions, or
designated contacts, a generator expresses what a human would do as a
human–object interaction 𝐱 \mathbf{x} (Sec. 3.1 ).
An agent then determines how the robot can realize it by proposing and refining contact programs through practice (Sec. 3.2 ).

指定联系人,生成者表达人类作为
human - 对象交互 x\ mathbf{x} (sec. 3. 1) 。
然后通过实践提出和完善接触程序来确定机器人如何实现(第3.2条)。

blocks.en:
We separate the task description from structured hand and finger
commands. To control the acting hand, we guide each denoising step
with low-dimensional, temporally interpolated body-pose offsets.
The guidance penalizes displacement of the stationary hand’s anchor
centroid and wrist, while attracting the acting hand toward an
object- and part-dependent contact prototype estimated from training
interactions. The offsets are optimized at sparse temporal knots and
interpolated across the motion window. The inactive arm joints are
additionally fixed to their observed configuration.

blocks.en:
We introduce a lightweight adapter for finger-specific motion
control without retraining the diffusion backbone.
Each control token encodes a finger identity and keyframe curl targets.
Trained on synthetic finger edits, the adapter injects
control residuals into the corresponding anatomical anchor tokens
and predicts finger-specific joint corrections.
Unlike direct joint interpolation, the learned edits account
for the surrounding hand–object motion, reducing implausible
hand poses and jitter.

手的姿势和颤抖。

At inference, two denoising trajectories share the same initial noise:
a reference branch with task-level text and hand-selection guidance,
and a branch with finger-control conditioning. We combine their
clean-motion predictions at each step: 𝐱 ^ 0 edit = 𝐱 ^ 0 ref + 𝐌 ℱ ⊙ ( 𝐱 ^ 0 ctrl − 𝐱 ^ 0 ref ) , \widehat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}^{\mathrm{edit}}=\widehat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}^{\mathrm{ref}}+\mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{F}}\odot\left(\widehat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}^{\mathrm{ctrl}}-\widehat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}^{\mathrm{ref}}\right), (2) where 𝐌 ℱ \mathbf{M}_{\mathcal{F}} selects the commanded finger
channels. This decoupled sampling preserves unconstrained body,
object, and hand motion while editing the specified fingers.

Finger articulation and finger contact impose distinct constraints.
Given a designated contacting set ℱ ⋆ \mathcal{F}^{\star} , we refine
the generated motion by optimizing temporal offsets on the acting
arm and fingers: min 𝚫 ℒ touch + ℒ pen + λ e ​ ℒ excl + λ a ​ ℒ smooth . \min_{\boldsymbol{\Delta}}\quad\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{touch}}+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{pen}}+\lambda_{e}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{excl}}+\lambda_{a}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{smooth}}. (3) The touch term attracts sampled distal pads of the designated fingers
to the moving-part surface during contact frames, using the articulated-part geometry. The penetration term
keeps the acting hand’s finger segments outside the moving part; for
exclusive-finger instructions, ℒ excl \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{excl}} additionally keeps non-designated fingers and the palm away from it; and ℒ smooth \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{smooth}} limits additional wrist and fingertip
acceleration. The refinement is applied post hoc to the sampled motion,
keeping the other hand, the torso, and the object fixed.
This allows contacts that never occur in the training data, such as

blocks.en: 3.2 Generation-Guided Agentic Manipulation
blocks.zh: 3.2 代指操纵剂

blocks.en:
To bridge HOI generation and dexterous robot manipulation,
FineDex treats generated interactions as actionable priors
rather than trajectories to replay.
The generated HOI provides hand roles, approach directions,
contact configurations, and target object articulation,
but may not satisfy the robot’s kinematic and physical constraints.
We therefore separate instruction constraints from motion guidance:
designated hands and fingers restrict admissible contact programs,
while the generated HOI guides contact selection and
support-hand placement.
An agent then adapts contact configurations and execution
parameters through test-time practice, without per-instance training.
Robot-specific constraints, such as an unavailable hand,
are incorporated into the digital twin.

为了沟通HOI的生成和机械操纵
FineDex 将生成的相互作用视为可诉前科
而不是重放的轨迹。

联系人配置以及目标对象表达,
但可能无法满足机器人的运动和身体限制。
因此,我们把指令限制与动议指导分开:
指定手和手指限制可允许的接触程序;
而生成的 HOI 引导联系人选择和
支持手插图。
一个代理然后修改联系人配置和执行
参数通过测试时间练习,不进行每次测试培训。
机器人特有的限制因素,例如手无寸铁,
纳入数字双胞胎。

blocks.en:
We retarget generated hand motion with an interaction mesh over hand
and object keypoints in the object frame, preserving its Laplacian
coordinates under joint-limit and non-penetration constraints. The
resulting wrist and finger references guide the construction and
evaluation of contact programs; replaying them unchanged is only one
program option.

without fixing the final contact poses or execution timing.

blocks.en: 3.3 FingerBench

blocks.en:
Conventional motion metrics do not assess whether
fine-grained instructions are followed.
FingerBench evaluates instruction compliance through two tracks.
The generation track evaluates hand selection (Switch/Still),
finger motion (A1–A5), and finger contact (B1–B4).
A1–A5 test single-finger motion, same- and opposite-direction
finger motions, bimanual control, and action timing.
Success requires the instructed motion while preserving
uncommanded fingers.
B1–B4 evaluate contact with the reference finger,
exclusive contact, counterfactual finger contact,
and thumb–index pinching.
Success requires the designated contact and corresponding
object articulation, with unintended contacts excluded
where specified.

finger-conditioned success rate (FC-SR) and Robo-SR.

by impulse share, while Robo-SR limits the duration
of unintended contacts by other hand regions.

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
ARCTIC [ 6 ] provides 3D body, hand, and object
motion for bimanual interactions with 11 articulated objects.
We split ARCTIC into training, validation, and test sets
and extract 32-frame windows with a stride of 16.
Each window is annotated with hand roles, finger-level contacts,
object-part regions, and articulation, first generated with
Gemini 3.8 and then verified with Claude, which corrected 497
of 13,472 annotations, mostly hand assignments and part references.

并取出32个框架的窗户,走16步。
每个窗口都带有手部角色 指层联系人
对象部分区域,并首先生成
双子座 3.8,然后与克洛德核实,纠正了497
* 包括13 472个说明,大部分是手工作业和部分参考资料。

blocks.en:
We evaluate HOI generation using standard metrics:
FID, R-precision (R@3), matching distance (MM-Dist),
diversity (Div), wrist error, average variance error (AVE),
contact ratio (CR), penetration (Pen), and foot skating (FS).
To assess fine-grained controllability, FingerBench
(Sec. 3.3 ) evaluates hand selection,
finger motion, and designated contacts.
Robotic execution is evaluated using task success,
finger-conditioned success rate (FC-SR), and Robo-SR
under randomized dynamics.

blocks.en:
As shown in Tab. 4 ,
FineDex improves task success over Astra-only planning
in every condition. The gains are consistent but modest:
across 174 shifted configurations, FineDex achieves 54.8 % 54.8\% task success, compared with 50.0 % 50.0\% without generated priors, with the same planning budget and no
retraining. The largest gain with floating hands occurs under
object-size variations ( 68.9 % 68.9\% vs. 59.6 % 59.6\% ).

blocks.en:
The generated HOI guides contact selection rather than
prescribing a trajectory to replay.
Only 21 % 21\% of committed programs directly reuse
the generated contacts; more often, the prior guides
the ranking of library and synthesized contacts
and the placement of the support hand.
Among 14 configurations that succeed in at least half
of the trials with priors but never without them,
10 use the generated support-hand pose to stabilize
the object, a strategy not found without the prior. Removing the grasp library as well leaves no human interaction data and lowers success to 59.4 % 59.4\% (floating) and 28.9 % 28.9\% (G1) in
Tab. 3 (a); no box trial then succeeds, since
geometric synthesis finds no contact that opens the lid.

blocks.en:
The importance of instruction-aligned priors is further
evident in Tab. 3 (b).
With finger instructions alone, the agent achieves 40.2 % 40.2\% task success and 19.4 % 19.4\% FC-SR.
Adding an unedited prior reduces these to 29.7 % 29.7\% and 15.2 % 15.2\% , respectively, as its suggested contacts
may conflict with the instructed finger.
In contrast, finger-edited priors restore task success
to 40.3 % 40.3\% and improve FC-SR to 24.4 % 24.4\% ,
with 60.5 % 60.5\% of successful trials using the
designated finger. These results highlight the importance of preserving
finger-level intent during robotic execution.

In Tab. 3 (a), directly replaying

The agent alone does not close this gap: executing its most

Success grows with the practice budget: stopping after one or
two of the four rounds yields 43.8 % 43.8\% and 57.0 % 57.0\% with floating
hands ( 25.0 % 25.0\% and 30.5 % 30.5\% on G1). Gains level off after about six.

blocks.en:
Fig. 6 demonstrates FineDex on a physical
Unitree G1 humanoid equipped with Wuji Hand 2.2,
covering finger-specific left-hand manipulation and
right-hand operation of an espresso machine and a microwave.
The contact programs selected through digital-twin practice
are transferred to the robot and executed open-loop
without online replanning.
To align the physical setup with simulation,
the digital twin selects a robot stance 𝐓 𝒫 \mathbf{T}^{\mathcal{P}} that maximizes the fraction of reachable, collision-free
wrist poses. The object is then placed at ( 𝐓 𝒫 ) − 1 ​ 𝐓 1 𝒪 (\mathbf{T}^{\mathcal{P}})^{-1}\mathbf{T}^{\mathcal{O}}_{1} in the pelvis frame, without further robot-side tuning.
Under a fixed object placement, the left-middle-finger
program succeeds in all five consecutive trials.
The digital twin uses the printed objects’ meshes and masses,
with control gains fixed across tasks.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented FineDex, a framework that makes finger-level intent
both expressible and executable. Trained on our fine-grained annotations, the generator produces coordinated human–object motion conditioned on hand, finger, and contact instructions. Rather than directly replaying generated motions,
an agent uses them as priors to discover executable contact
behaviors through test-time practice. Experiments demonstrate
state-of-the-art fine-grained controllability and HOI generation
quality, substantial gains in dexterous manipulation success,
and successful execution on a real humanoid robot.
We further introduce FingerBench to evaluate instruction
following in both generation and physical execution.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了FineDex, 一个框架 使手指层次的意图
可表达性和可执行性。 这台发电机以精细的笔记训练, 而不是直接重播产生的运动,
代理以它们作为发现可执行联系人的前科
通过测试时间实践的行为. 实验证明
最先进的精细可控性和HOI一代
质量, 大幅度提高 狡猾的操纵成功,
和成功执行 一个真正的人造机器人。
我们还引进了Finger Bench来评估指示
既执行又执行

blocks.en:
Enforcing designated-finger constraints reduces task success,
while limited arm reach and imperfect wrist tracking remain
major failure modes on the humanoid.
Real-robot behaviors are executed open loop, without
online feedback; closing this loop is left to future work.

手臂伸展有限,手腕跟踪不完善
人体的主要故障模式。
Real- Robot 行为被执行打开循环, 不
在线反馈; 关闭此循环留给未来工作.
